**Decision: CONTINUE.** Round 425 is part 2 of the current regression (REGRESSION-2026-11-10). A changes nothing; C does a browser sweep on the new baseline `f6c76f4`.

**Round 424, from C's evidence:** C passed it: 9 rows, 0 bugs, browser-verified. I checked the perf results myself: all 17 drag perf checks that failed in round 423 are back at their expected values. The gate published it as `f6c76f4` (264 test files, 3,957 tests, no Medium or worse in review). So:
- C-R423-01 is closed, and PERF-11c-iii-e-ii is back to მზადაა.
- A's two Lows and one info note on my own mutant file go to `deferred_low_polish`.
- The reviewer's architecture note becomes a backlog signal, SIG-R424-BOUNDARY-FIBER-GUARD: a guard for lane boundary changes, for RETRO 435. It is not scheduled as a task. I also attached it to the open STEM-LANES architecture checkpoint request, because STEM-LANES touches the same lane code.

**Round 425 covers:**
- **Everything finished up to round 390:** round 389's rows (rounds 343–388) and round 390's rows (up to 342, plus the parked rows), run as one round. Last time these took C 1.4 h, but the same template has taken 3.6 h before, so I estimate up to about 4.6 h against the 350-minute job limit. If time runs out, the round is PARTIAL and resumes from its progress file.
- **A lane re-check on the new baseline:** `ArrangementLane` changed after part 1, and round 424 did not re-run clip virtualization or lane waveforms, so those run again against part 1's outputs.
- **The four checks carried from the last regression, now ruled:**
  - **NO-SHIFT-203** is retired. Its reference tree no longer exists, and an existing focus-style check (RS-4B) covers only part of it. A record-only box capture of the rest becomes the next regression's reference.
  - **The four outdated test scripts** run from round 390's already-adapted copies.
  - **The page glitch on `/studio/middle-east` seen once in round 390** gets its own row: 4 fresh loads per viewport, with nothing else running.
  - **The video-sound check** is measured from the clip's real grid-snapped start.
- **Rulings for older checks:** library previews now stream, so a preview may sound before decoding ends; it passes if it plays once and stops on Play. Two memory and eviction numbers recorded before round 391 are now recorded rather than asserted. A difference C can trace to a named round 391–424 goes to me to rule; an untraced one is a finding.
- **Perf, smoke and auth:**
  - The full perf suite is not re-run: the published code is byte-identical to what C verified in round 424 (`b-round-424/rrperf-carry-proof.txt`).
  - The perf-lib unit tests, the smoke test and the auth guard run again. I ran the auth URLs once myself at the baseline: no header gives 401, a bare request gives 400.
  - The fake-token auth path stays BLOCKED because there is no backend in the cloud.
- **After a clean pass:** `regression-last.json` is updated, then STEM-LANES if Saba answers (`AGREE-STEM-LANES.md` is still `awaiting_user`), otherwise SYS-2 stage 2a.

**Files I wrote:**
- `tasks/round-424.md` (a copy; nothing deleted)
- `current-task.md` (round 425)
- `backlog.json` v401 (D-29z1483 to D-29z1486)
- `feature-status.md`
- `b-round-424.md`
- `b-next.json`
- `b-round-424/`: the claims script and its output (no errors), the frozen tree, the perf carry proof and checkpoint

No app source was touched; the store tree is clean.

The advisor was available and I consulted it twice. Before planning, it caught that part 2 also had to include rounds 343–388. Before close, it found gaps in my draft, and I fixed all of them before finishing.
